section_summary.extract_value: Discussion summarizes a single cross-sectional study (referred to as 'the present study' and 'this is the first study...') that examined links between early memories of warmth/safeness, self-compassion, body appreciation, and eating psychopathology in a nonclinical sample composed only of female participants. The model explained substantial variance in eating psychopathology, with self-compassion and body appreciation mediating the effect of early positive experiences on disordered eating; limitations include cross-sectional design, self-report measures, female-only and nonclinical sample, and lack of generalizability.
section_summary.evidence_source: Key sentences: 'However, to the extent of our knowledge, this is the first study that examined the relationship...'; 'the sample of this study only comprised female participants'; 'use of a nonclinical sample'; 'while controlling the effects of age and BMI'; 'Path analysis's findings showed that the tested model revealed an excellent fit... accounting 49% of the variance of eating psychopathology severity.'
